sources.data/derived/mars_terrain.json: slopes of the sites and of the Earth squares (agent MARS-TERRAIN): MOLA MEGDR and ETOPO 2022
sources.data/derived/mars_climate.json: Sun, climate and the cannot-match list of the sites; climate and bare ground of the Earth squares (agent MARS-CLIMATE): NASA POWER (MERRA-2), ESA WorldCover 2021, Mars Climate Database, Phoenix MET data from NASA's PDS archive, and Curiosity REMS figures from NASA's public weather feed, which says it is for outreach, not archive data

sites_base_meta.what: The Mars sites of the Mars part (plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-14-mars-part.md): the nine places where a NASA lander or rover landed and worked (Viking 1, Viking 2, Mars Pathfinder, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, Curiosity at Gale, InSight, Perseverance at Jezero), and three mid-latitude ice regions studied for human landings.
sites_base_meta.made_by: agent MARS-SITES, by reading the saved sources in data/raw/mars_sites/; written by build_mars_sites_base.py in the MARS-SITES scratch folder (not a project script)
sites_base_meta.how: Each latitude and longitude is copied as written in one saved source file (meta.coordinates names the file and the exact text); nothing is averaged or moved. Pages were downloaded on 2026-11-14 with User-Agent twinfinder/0.1; data/raw/mars_sites/_downloads.tsv lists every URL and time.
sites_base_meta.convention: planetocentric latitude (degrees, north positive), longitude 0 to 360 degrees east
sites_base_meta.convention_note: The USGS gazetteer (planetocentric) and the PDS Phoenix page (areocentric) state their system. The other coordinate sources give east longitude without naming the latitude system; they are kept as written. If one were planetographic, its planetocentric latitude would be smaller by the amount in meta.coordinates[id].if_it_were_planetographic_deg (IAU 2000 ellipsoid, 3396.19 by 3376.20 km), at most 0.33 degree, well inside the 2 x 2 degree site box.
sites_base_meta.status: NASA has not selected a human landing site on Mars. Arcadia Planitia and Deuteronilus Mensae are candidates that were studied: exploration zones proposed at NASA's First Landing Site/Exploration Zone Workshop for Human Missions to the Surface of Mars (27-30 October 2015, Lunar and Planetary Institute, Houston; 47 proposals), and regions named in NASA's release on the NASA-funded SWIM ice maps (8 February 2021). Phlegra Montes (site PM-1) comes from a 2021 abstract of JPL, SpaceX and university authors (Golombek et al. 2021, LPSC abstract 2420) on landing sites for SpaceX Starship; it is a study, not a NASA selection. No other commercial list was used. The second pass adds the other six sites of the 2021 shortlist and the exploration zones proposed at the 2015 workshop. A proposal or a study is not a NASA decision.

sites.name: Jezero crater, Perseverance landing site (Octavia E. Butler Landing)
sites.kind: visited by a NASA mission
sites.why: NASA's Perseverance rover landed here on 18 February 2021, on the floor of a crater that once held a lake and a river delta, and its MEDA station measures the weather at the surface.

sources.what: HiRISE (NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter) image ESP_068360_1985, Perseverance on the ground, 25 February 2021: image centre 18.442 N, 77.452 E
Rodriguez-Manfredi et al. 2023, Nature Geoscience 16, 19-28 (MEDA, first 250 sols): landed at 18.44 N 77.45 E
USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Jezero: crater centre 18.41 N, 77.69 E, 47.52 km across (planetocentric, east, 0-360)

Mustard 2015, abstract 1034, First Landing Site/Exploration Zone Workshop for Human Missions to the Surface of Mars: the Jezero crater open-basin lake and delta, also proposed as a human exploration zone

sun.how: By formula from the site's latitude (planetocentric) and the tilt of Mars, 25.19 degrees: over the Mars year the Sun's declination runs between -25.19 and +25.19 degrees; noon Sun height = 90 - |latitude - declination|, so the lowest is 90 - (|latitude| + 25.19) (below 0: polar night) and the highest is 90 where |latitude| <= 25.19, else 90 - (|latitude| - 25.19). Day length = 2 H0 / 360 x 24.66 h, with cos H0 = -tan(latitude) tan(declination), at declination -25.19 and +25.19 (0 h in polar night, 24.66 h in polar day). A Mars solar day is 24.66 Earth hours. The Sun's centre on a flat horizon, no refraction, no terrain; the unequal length of the Mars seasons (orbit eccentricity 0.093) changes when, not how high.

sites.name: Arcadia Planitia (Erebus Montes exploration zone)
sites.kind: studied for a human landing
sites.why: Smooth northern plains thought to hold abundant water ice within the top metre of the ground, studied as a candidate exploration zone for human landings at NASA's 2015 workshop (Viola, McEwen and Dundas) and named by NASA's SWIM ice-mapping project as a region of accessible shallow ice, but not selected by NASA.

sources.what: Viola, McEwen and Dundas 2015, abstract 1011, First Landing Site/Exploration Zone Workshop for Human Missions to the Surface of Mars: Erebus Montes EZ centred near 192.1 E, 39.0 N

Bussey and Hoffman 2016 (NASA), Human Mars Landing Site and Impacts on Mars Surface Operations, Appendix D: the 47 proposed exploration zones
NASA/JPL release of 8 February 2021 on the SWIM maps (Morgan et al. 2021, Nature Astronomy): names the plains of Arcadia Planitia for accessible subsurface ice

sun.how: By formula from the site's latitude (planetocentric) and the tilt of Mars, 25.19 degrees: over the Mars year the Sun's declination runs between -25.19 and +25.19 degrees; noon Sun height = 90 - |latitude - declination|, so the lowest is 90 - (|latitude| + 25.19) (below 0: polar night) and the highest is 90 where |latitude| <= 25.19, else 90 - (|latitude| - 25.19). Day length = 2 H0 / 360 x 24.66 h, with cos H0 = -tan(latitude) tan(declination), at declination -25.19 and +25.19 (0 h in polar night, 24.66 h in polar day). A Mars solar day is 24.66 Earth hours. The Sun's centre on a flat horizon, no refraction, no terrain; the unequal length of the Mars seasons (orbit eccentricity 0.093) changes when, not how high.

sites.why: New impact craters show clean ice only 0.15 m below the surface, and the site has no hazards in a landing ellipse of 25 km.

sources.what: Stoker and Heldmann 2015, abstract 1018, First Landing Site/Exploration Zone Workshop for Human Missions to the Surface of Mars: Amazonis Planitia mid-latitude ice; position as written: Location of ROI: 40-50 N, 160 -190 E ; Specific Landing Site proposed: 46.16N, 188.8 E

sites.position_kind: landing site, stated

sun.how: By formula from the site's latitude (planetocentric) and the tilt of Mars, 25.19 degrees: over the Mars year the Sun's declination runs between -25.19 and +25.19 degrees; noon Sun height = 90 - |latitude - declination|, so the lowest is 90 - (|latitude| + 25.19) (below 0: polar night) and the highest is 90 where |latitude| <= 25.19, else 90 - (|latitude| - 25.19). Day length = 2 H0 / 360 x 24.66 h, with cos H0 = -tan(latitude) tan(declination), at declination -25.19 and +25.19 (0 h in polar night, 24.66 h in polar day). A Mars solar day is 24.66 Earth hours. The Sun's centre on a flat horizon, no refraction, no terrain; the unequal length of the Mars seasons (orbit eccentricity 0.093) changes when, not how high.

sun.how: By formula from the site's latitude (planetocentric) and the tilt of Mars, 25.19 degrees: over the Mars year the Sun's declination runs between -25.19 and +25.19 degrees; noon Sun height = 90 - |latitude - declination|, so the lowest is 90 - (|latitude| + 25.19) (below 0: polar night) and the highest is 90 where |latitude| <= 25.19, else 90 - (|latitude| - 25.19). Day length = 2 H0 / 360 x 24.66 h, with cos H0 = -tan(latitude) tan(declination), at declination -25.19 and +25.19 (0 h in polar night, 24.66 h in polar day). A Mars solar day is 24.66 Earth hours. The Sun's centre on a flat horizon, no refraction, no terrain; the unequal length of the Mars seasons (orbit eccentricity 0.093) changes when, not how high.
